title: Sequencer Batch Conservator: workload fingerprinting, safe gradual-apply, and conservative heuristics
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Build the 'Sequencer Batch Conservator'—a recommendation engine that generates conservative batching and KV-cache parameter changes based on continuous workload fingerprints, and applies them via a staged safe-apply flow with automated rollback triggers. This ticket covers profiling heuristics, candidate scoring, shadow evaluation harness, staged rollout orchestration, and operator observability integration.

Motivation: Many customers see cost improvements from more aggressive coalescing and prefix caching, but applying aggressive batch configs in production causes tail-latency regressions for a minority of request shapes. We need an engine that: 1) surfaces high-confidence batch/cache parameter tweaks per workload cohort, 2) validates them via shadow/shape-simulated evaluation and canaries, and 3) applies changes gradually with automatic rollback if a configurable set of SLO/cost-quality signals degrade.

Scope: profiling pipeline (fingerprints, heatmaps), heuristic candidate generator (safe defaults + conservative multipliers), offline shadow-eval harness (simulated KV/cache/k-merging), in-cluster staged apply controller (shadow->canary->ramp->global), telemetry hooks (per-candidate metrics, A/B tagging), and runbook for manual intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint pipeline emits workload cohort ids and 24h signature histograms to TSDB
Recommendation engine produces ranked candidate configs with confidence scores and expected cost delta
Shadow-eval harness can run candidate config against 1M sample requests with simulated KV cache to estimate latency 95/99 and token cost impact
Staged apply controller implements shadow -> 1% canary -> 10% ramp -> 100% rollout with automatic rollback on SLO or error-rate thresholds
Console surfaces per-candidate dashboard: estimated savings, measured delta during canary, and rollback reason if triggered
E2E tests for rollback logic and canary tagging integrated in CI
design_notes: High-level design: 1) Fingerprinter: lightweight rolling-window sketch that captures: mean sequence length, prefix reuse rate, KV cache hit-rate estimate, request arrival burstiness, and prompt template signatures. Use reservoir sampling to retain representative requests for shadow runs. 2) Candidate generator: start from current config and propose conservative steps (e.g., microbatch_size *1.2, max_batch_window -10ms) plus an aggressive variant for lab-only experiments. 3) Scoring: cost_score (expected token cost reduction), risk_score (estimated increase in p99 latency, tail amplification factor), and confidence based on sample size and jitter. 4) Shadow-eval: replay reservoir through runtime with candidate config in isolated path, record simulated queueing and KV hits. 5) Apply controller: integrates with rollout service; uses canary traffic splitting and continuous metrics checks. 6) Telemetry: tag requests with candidate_id during canary and emit delta metrics per model/route. 7) Safety: all candidates must pass 'no-p99-regression' and 'error-rate < baseline*1.2' in shadow before canary.
implementation_plan: Phase 2: Candidate generator and scoring + local sim harness (2 wks)
Phase 3: Shadow-eval integration with runtime (3 wks)
Phase 4: Staged-apply controller + console instrumentation (3 wks)
Phase 5: E2E tests, runbook, and pilot with two low-risk customers (2 wks)
rollout_plan: Default rollout: shadow for 24h -> automated 1% canary for 1h -> evaluate metrics -> if pass, ramp to 10% over 30m -> hold 2h -> if pass, 100% over 2h. Operator override allowed at any stage. Canary tagging will be immutable and visible in tracing. Temporal circuit-breakers: if p99 increases by >15% or error rate increases >0.5pp for the canary cohort, immediate rollback to previous config. Cost-saving gating: require >= 3% expected token-cost reduction for non-experimental candidates.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback triggers: 1) p99 latency regresses beyond configured threshold, 2) error-rate spike above configured threshold, 3) tail-quality signal from model-eval webhooks (e.g., hallucination score increase). Rollback flow: mark candidate failed, revert config in routing layer, emit incident to #runtime-ops with diagnostics bundle, and create follow-up action item in Linear. For partial rollbacks (ramp stage), automatically reduce traffic to previous step instead of full revert when regression is marginal. All rollbacks must include delta metrics snapshot and a best-effort repro trace link.

2026-02-27 - Connor Liu: PoC fingerprinter complete. Reservoir samples are representative for 97% of routes; outliers exist for low-volume interactive flows.
2026-03-02 - Lina Gomez (SRE): We need a hard guard to prevent applying aggressive configs to routes with <1000 requests/day. Added as a hard rule in the candidate generator.
2026-03-05 - QA: Shadow-eval harness integrated; initial runs show cost estimate bias ~5% due to simulation of KV warmup — adjusting simulation warmup window.
2026-03-09 - Product (Arjun Rao): Add UI column for 'expected user-visible delta' and link to prompt-set evaluation. Marking for Console Q2 roadmap discussion.
2026-03-10 - Connor Liu: Started work on canary tagging; next: connect rollout controller to observability alerts.
notes_for_reviewers: Look for edge-cases: bursty prompt patterns, multi-tenant noise where samples cross-cohort boundaries, and routes with high variance in sequence length. Review scoring weights for cost vs. risk — currently tuned conservatively but will need dynamic adjustment after initial pilots.
